verdicts.corrected_claim: The ING candidate contains 40 files and 11,464 lines at both revisions. Orchestrator-owned state drives firehose, comment and CI polling; the comment path already performs I/O asynchronously and folds a correlated result back into State. Cursor, ETag, reconciliation and cadence fields remain in that state, so moving ownership out of the orchestration loop is a justified design direction. A dedicated listeners supervisor is an option, not a proven prerequisite for library packaging or a requirement to create exactly one process per source.
verdicts.method: Enumerated ING files from the retained taxonomy and independent AST module inventory. Read orchestrator/comment_polling.ex:1-10,35-60 and start_async/apply_async/apply_async_started; apply_async checks the poll reference before updating State. Read ci_lifecycle.ex:379-451 and the GithubCIPoller invocation, dispatcher.ex:133 and command_scan.ex, and the listed fields in state.ex:289-316. Checked event poller modules own fetch logic while results/cursors pass through Orchestrator state. This reproduces the responsibilities independently of the report graph.
verdicts.note: The finding supports separating poll scheduling/state from dispatch. The original "not cuttable" and "must come first" wording mistakes one migration strategy for a structural impossibility: a library can accept state and return results before a process migration. Any new owner must preserve stale-result rejection, rate-limit floors, pagination/reconciliation, cursor persistence and event ordering. This check did not measure delay caused by any source.
